title: Question 2: Temporary Appointments on the Commission on Judicial Disabilities

context.text: Placed on the ballot by the General Assembly as a legislatively referred constitutional amendment, Chapter 878 of the 2026 legislative session (Senate Bill 933), per the State Board of Elections' ballot question page.

question.text: Temporary Appointments on the Commission on Judicial Disabilities: Authorizing temporary substitute appointments to the Commission on Judicial Disabilities when a member is recused or disqualified, or when a member's term expires. In these situations, the Commission Chair may recall a former member of the Commission, or the Governor, at the request of the Commission Chair, may appoint a temporary substitute member or extend the term of a current member until a permanent replacement is appointed. Only individuals who meet the constitutional eligibility requirements may be recalled or appointed to the Commission. (Amending Article IV of the Maryland Constitution)

summary.text: The amendment would amend Article IV of the Maryland Constitution to allow temporary substitute appointments to the Commission on Judicial Disabilities when a member is recused or disqualified or a member's term expires. The Commission Chair could recall a former member, or the Governor, at the Chair's request, could appoint a temporary substitute or extend a current member's term until a permanent replacement is appointed; only people who meet the constitutional eligibility requirements could serve.

measure.yesMeans: A vote FOR this amendment means that temporary appointments to the Commission are allowed if a member is recused, disqualified, or if a member's term ends without a replacement. The Commission Chair can temporarily fill an opening on the Commission with a former member. The Governor can, at the request of the Commission Chair pick a temporary substitute to fill an opening on the Commission or extend the term of a current member until a replacement is appointed. Only individuals who meet the constitutional eligibility requirements may be recalled or appointed to the Commission.
measure.noMeans: A vote AGAINST the amendment means that current membership rules for the Commission stay the same. Temporary appointments are not allowed if a member is recused, disqualified, or if a member's term ends.

currentLaw.text: Under Article IV, Sections 4A and 4B of the Maryland Constitution the 11-member Commission on Judicial Disabilities (3 judges, 3 lawyers, 5 public members, appointed by the Governor with Senate consent) investigates complaints against judges. After a member's term expires the Commission may continue to conduct business with that member serving until the Governor appoints a replacement; vacancies are filled by the Governor for the unexpired term. Under Maryland Rule 18-411 a majority is a quorum if it includes at least one judge, one attorney and one public member, and where recusals or vacancies leave a proceeding without that mix the Supreme Court of Maryland may, with the written consent of the judge who is the subject, designate a substitute.

fiscalImpact.text: Department of Legislative Services fiscal and policy note on SB 933 (Third Reader): if voters approve, the Commission on Judicial Disabilities experiences operational efficiencies; there is otherwise no material impact on State finances or operations. Local effect: none.
